title: VIP Chapter 6 Week 6: Soils, Natural Vegetation and Wildlife Resources of Ethiopia and The Horn

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a factor influencing the rate of chemical weathering in Ethiopia?
questions.correct_answer: C) Wind speed
questions.explanation: Correct: Wind speed primarily affects mechanical (physical) weathering, not chemical. A, B, and D are wrong—they all directly influence chemical weathering rates. Temperature speeds reactions, parent material determines susceptibility, and rainfall provides water for reactions.

questions.text: Ethiopian highland soils typically have higher organic matter content than lowland soils. This is primarily because:
options: A) There is more livestock in the lowlands
B) Lower temperatures slow organic matter decomposition in highlands
C) Lowland soils are more fertile
D) Highland soils receive less rainfall
questions.correct_answer: B) Lower temperatures slow organic matter decomposition in highlands
questions.explanation: Correct: Cooler highland temperatures slow decomposition, preserving organic matter. A is wrong—livestock can reduce organic matter. C is wrong—lowland soils are generally less fertile. D is wrong—highlands receive more rainfall, not less.

questions.text: What is the relationship between Ethiopia's soil policies and food security?
options: B) Soil policies directly determine agricultural productivity and food availability
D) Policies have minimal impact on food security
questions.correct_answer: B) Soil policies directly determine agricultural productivity and food availability
questions.explanation: Correct: Soil management is fundamental to agricultural output. A is wrong—there is a direct relationship. C is wrong—irrigation is only one aspect. D is wrong—policies significantly impact food security.

questions.text: In which Ethiopian region would you most likely find Solonchaks (saline soils)?
questions.correct_answer: B) Afar Depression
questions.explanation: Correct: Afar has arid conditions with salt accumulation. A is wrong—Bale has high rainfall. C is wrong—Simien is cold and wet. D is wrong—Kaffa has humid conditions with deep red soils.

questions.text: The primary reason for Ethiopia's high soil erosion rate is:
options: C) Combination of deforestation, overgrazing, and steep terrain
questions.correct_answer: C) Combination of deforestation, overgrazing, and steep terrain
questions.explanation: Correct: Multiple factors interact to cause high erosion. A is wrong—topography alone is not the cause. B is wrong—climate change exacerbates but isn't the primary cause. D is wrong—urbanization is not the main factor.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian soil type is characterized by high shrink-swell capacity and self-cracking when dry?
questions.correct_answer: B) Vertisols
questions.explanation: Correct: Vertisols have >50% clay causing shrink-swell. A is wrong—Nitisols are stable. C is wrong—Fluvisols don't crack. D is wrong—Cambisols have moderate clay.

questions.text: The economic implication of soil degradation in Ethiopia is mainly:
options: A) Reduced agricultural productivity and food insecurity
questions.correct_answer: A) Reduced agricultural productivity and food insecurity
questions.explanation: Correct: Degradation reduces yields and threatens food security. B is wrong—degradation doesn't increase tourism. C is wrong—oil prices are unrelated. D is wrong—degradation doesn't improve industry.

questions.text: Which conservation practice is most effective for steep slopes in Ethiopia?
questions.correct_answer: B) Terracing
questions.explanation: Correct: Terracing effectively controls erosion on steep slopes. A is wrong—contour plowing helps on moderate slopes. C is wrong—strip cropping works on gentle slopes. D is wrong—mulching is for moisture conservation.

questions.text: What is the impact of deforestation on Ethiopian soils?
options: B) Accelerates erosion and reduces organic matter
questions.correct_answer: B) Accelerates erosion and reduces organic matter
questions.explanation: Correct: Deforestation exposes soil to erosion and removes organic inputs. A is wrong—deforestation reduces fertility. C is wrong—there is significant impact. D is wrong—deforestation reduces water retention.

questions.text: Which measure addresses both soil conservation and livelihood improvement in Ethiopia?
options: B) Community-based watershed management with livelihood support
questions.correct_answer: B) Community-based watershed management with livelihood support
questions.explanation: Correct: This approach combines conservation with economic benefits. A is wrong—importing food doesn't address soil. C is wrong—urbanization often degrades soils. D is wrong—roads don't conserve soil.

questions.text: The characteristic dark color of Ethiopian Vertisols is primarily due to:
options: B) High organic matter and clay content
questions.correct_answer: B) High organic matter and clay content
questions.explanation: Correct: Organic matter and clay give dark color. A is wrong—iron oxides give red color (Nitisols). C is wrong—calcium carbonate gives white. D is wrong—silica gives light colors.

questions.text: What is the main difference between Nitisols and Cambisols in terms of agricultural potential?
options: A) Both have the same potential
B) Nitisols are better for coffee while Cambisols are more general purpose
C) Cambisols are better for irrigation
questions.correct_answer: B) Nitisols are better for coffee while Cambisols are more general purpose
questions.explanation: Correct: Nitisols specialize in coffee/tea, Cambisols are general cereals. A is wrong—they differ. C is wrong—Fluvisols are better for irrigation. D is wrong—Nitisols are not saline.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian soil degradation problem is most severe in the Rift Valley?
questions.correct_answer: B) Salinization
questions.explanation: Correct: Rift Valley has irrigation-induced salinity. A is wrong—acidification is in western highlands. C is wrong—compaction is common in Vertisols. D is wrong—waterlogging occurs in some irrigated areas but salinization is more widespread.

questions.text: The broad-bed and furrow (BBF) technique is specifically designed for:
questions.correct_answer: B) Vertisols management
questions.explanation: Correct: BBF improves drainage in high-clay Vertisols. A is wrong—Nitisols are well-drained. C is wrong—sandy soils need different management. D is wrong—saline reclamation uses leaching.

questions.text: What is the MOST significant long-term impact of nutrient depletion in Ethiopian soils?
options: A) Reduced agricultural yields and food insecurity
questions.correct_answer: A) Reduced agricultural yields and food insecurity
questions.explanation: Correct: Nutrient depletion directly reduces yields. B is wrong—this is a more extreme outcome. C is wrong—this is a symptom, not the impact. D is wrong—biodiversity loss is important but not the most significant impact.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a biological soil conservation measure in Ethiopia?
questions.correct_answer: B) Planting cover crops
questions.explanation: Correct: Cover crops are biological measures. A, C, and D are wrong—they are mechanical/physical measures. Biological measures involve living organisms.

questions.text: Ethiopia's Green Legacy Initiative's contribution to soil conservation is primarily through:
options: A) Reducing erosion and increasing organic matter
questions.correct_answer: A) Reducing erosion and increasing organic matter
questions.explanation: Correct: Trees reduce erosion and add organic matter. B is wrong—exporting timber is not the main purpose. C is wrong—urban development is not tree planting. D is wrong—industry is not the focus.

questions.text: The relationship between Ethiopia's highland soils and the Nile River system is:
options: A) Soil erosion in highlands contributes to siltation of the Blue Nile
C) The Nile improves Ethiopian soils
D) Soils don't affect the Nile
questions.correct_answer: A) Soil erosion in highlands contributes to siltation of the Blue Nile
questions.explanation: Correct: Highland erosion affects downstream sedimentation. B is wrong—there is a direct connection. C is wrong—the Nile doesn't improve soils. D is wrong—soils directly affect the Nile.

questions.text: Which agronomic practice helps maintain soil fertility in Ethiopian highlands?
questions.correct_answer: B) Crop rotation including legumes
questions.explanation: Correct: Legumes fix nitrogen, maintaining fertility. A is wrong—monoculture depletes nutrients. C is wrong—burning loses organic matter. D is wrong—overgrazing degrades soil.

questions.text: The success of soil conservation in Tigray demonstrates that:
options: A) Conservation is impossible in Ethiopia
B) Community participation and integrated approaches can reverse degradation
C) Only modern machinery can save soils
D) Conservation is not economically viable
questions.correct_answer: B) Community participation and integrated approaches can reverse degradation
questions.explanation: Correct: Tigray's success proves community action works. A is wrong—Tigray shows it's possible. C is wrong—traditional methods proved effective. D is wrong—conservation is economically beneficial.
